# AES Control Module Specification

## 1. Purpose

This module is the main controller for the AES unit. It decides when the cipher core may start processing a data block, when output data may be released, when key, IV, and data registers must be cleared, and how the PRNG is used for register clearing and reseeding. It also tracks whether complete key, IV, input, and output blocks have been supplied by software, and it generates the corresponding status and trigger-clearing behavior.

The module does not perform AES encryption/decryption itself. It only controls and observes the surrounding registers, the cipher core, and the PRNG.

## 2. Idle Behavior and Software Updates

When the module is idle, it must:

- Indicate that it is idle.
- Accept software updates to the key registers, IV registers, and control register.
- Forward key and IV write events so that complete key and IV blocks can be recognized.
- Accept control register updates only if the control register has no storage error and the module is idle.
- Ignore software writes to key and IV registers whenever the module is not idle.
- Track software writes to the input data registers at any time, including while an operation is in progress, so that the next input block can be staged in advance.
- Track software reads of the output data registers at any time, so that the module knows when a previous output block has been fully consumed.

A control register update must cause all previously tracked key, IV, and input-data write activity to be invalidated. After such an update, software must write all required registers again before a new block can be processed.

If the control register has a storage error, the module must:

- Treat the configuration as invalid.
- Not allow further control register updates.
- Not start any automatic or manual cipher operation.

## 3. Operation Start Conditions

The module must start cipher operations only when the configuration is valid and no fatal alert condition is present.

A configuration is valid when:

- A supported cipher mode is selected.
- The control register has no storage error.
- No fatal alert has been asserted.

### 3.1 Automatic Operation

In automatic mode, the module must start an operation when all of the following conditions are met:

- A complete key block has been written since the last control register update or key usage.
- A complete input data block has been written since the last control register update, data load, or data clear.
- For CBC, CFB, OFB, and CTR modes, a complete IV block must also be available.
- For CTR mode, the internal counter must additionally be ready.
- For ECB mode, no IV is required.

The module must not automatically start with a partially written key, IV, or input data block.

### 3.2 Manual Operation

In manual mode, the module must start an operation only when the start trigger is asserted and the configuration is valid. Manual mode must ignore the key, IV, input data, and counter readiness conditions. This allows software to force an operation for test or side-channel measurement purposes.

When a start trigger is accepted, the module must clear the trigger unless the operation first requires the decryption key to be generated.

### 3.3 Decryption Key Generation

For ECB or CBC decryption with a key that has not yet been expanded for decryption, the module must first cause the cipher core to generate the decryption start key before any data block is processed. During this key-generation phase:

- The actual data path must not consume the input data block.
- The manual start trigger must remain pending until the normal data operation actually begins.
- Key, IV, and data-in status must be updated only after the key-generation phase completes.

## 4. Data Loading and Processing

When an operation starts, the module must:

- Select the correct data source for the cipher core according to cipher mode and operation direction.
- For CBC decryption and for CFB, OFB, and CTR modes, capture the current input data block for later feedback use.
- For CFB, OFB, and CTR modes, ensure that the cipher core operates on the IV or counter value rather than directly on the input data.
- For CBC encryption, CFB encryption/decryption, OFB, and CTR modes, combine the IV or counter value with the input data as required by the mode.
- For CBC decryption, allow the IV to be applied after the cipher operation.

After the cipher core has accepted the block, the module must mark the key, IV, and input data as consumed, as appropriate to the mode and operation.

While the cipher core is processing, the module must continue to accept software writes to the input data registers so that a subsequent input block can be prepared. It must also continue to accept reads of the output data registers so that a previous output block can be drained.

## 5. PRNG Data Refresh

The module must request fresh pseudo-random data from the PRNG after each block is loaded into the cipher core. This data is needed for clearing internal state during the final cipher round and for clearing registers when software requests a clear.

If a clear request is pending while the cipher core is still processing, the module must finish the current cipher operation before performing the clear.

## 6. Completion and Output Handling

When the cipher core produces an output block, the module must decide whether to accept it based on the output-read status and the selected operation mode.

### 6.1 Automatic Mode

In automatic mode, the module must not overwrite an output block that has not yet been fully read by software. If a new output block is ready while a previous output block is still unread, the module must stall. It must set the stall indication and must not release the new output data until all output registers of the previous block have been read.

Once the previous output block has been fully read, the module must:

- Write the new output block to the output data registers.
- Indicate that output data is valid and available for reading.
- If a clear request is pending, defer the clear until after the output block is accepted.

### 6.2 Manual Mode

In manual mode, the module must not stall because of unread output data. It must accept a new output block even if the previous output block has not been read. If this causes previous output data to be overwritten while unread, the module must set the output-lost status.

### 6.3 IV Updates After Completion

After a cipher operation completes, the module must update the IV registers as required by the cipher mode:

- CBC encryption: IV becomes the output ciphertext block.
- CBC decryption: IV becomes the previous input data block.
- CFB encryption: IV becomes the output ciphertext block.
- CFB decryption: IV becomes the previous input data block.
- OFB mode: IV becomes the raw cipher output block, before it is XORed with the input data.
- CTR mode: IV is updated by the internal counter during the cipher operation, not only at completion.

After the IV is updated, the module must consider the IV available again for a subsequent operation only when the update is complete.

## 7. Register Clearing

When software asserts a key/IV/data-input clear request, the module must:

- Obtain fresh pseudo-random data from the PRNG.
- Overwrite all initial key registers, IV registers, and input data registers, including the previous-input-data register, with pseudo-random data.
- Cause the cipher core to clear its internal key material.
- Wait for confirmation that the clearing has completed.
- Clear the key/IV/data-input clear trigger.

When software asserts an output-data clear request, the module must:

- Obtain fresh pseudo-random data from the PRNG.
- Overwrite all output data registers with pseudo-random data.
- Wait for confirmation that the clearing has completed.
- Clear the output-data clear trigger.

If both clear requests are asserted together, the module must perform both clearing operations. It must not clear the triggers until both have completed successfully.

Clear requests asserted while an operation is in progress must be serviced after the current operation finishes.

## 8. PRNG Reseed

When software asserts a PRNG reseed request, the module must:

- Request a reseed from the PRNG.
- Wait for the PRNG to acknowledge the reseed.
- Clear the reseed trigger.
- Return to idle.

The reseed request must take priority over starting a new operation or performing register clearing while the module is idle.

## 9. Status Indications

The module must generate the following status information:

- **Idle**: Indicates that no operation, clear, or reseed sequence is in progress and no start request is being processed.
- **Input ready**: Indicates that no complete input data block is currently pending. Software may write a new input data block.
- **Output valid**: Indicates that an output data block has been written and is available to be read by software.
- **Stall**: Indicates that the cipher core has produced output data, but the module is preventing it from being written because the previous output block has not been read in automatic mode.
- **Output lost**: Indicates that an output data block was overwritten before all of its registers had been read. This can occur only in manual mode.

The module must clear the output-valid indication when all output registers have been read or when the output data is cleared. The output-lost indication must be cleared whenever the control register is updated.

## 10. Security and Fault Behavior

The module must continuously validate all internal control encodings, handshake signals, and mux selectors that it uses. If any of these values become invalid, or if the life-cycle controller requests escalation, the module must:

- Stop accepting new operations.
- Stop releasing output data or any write-enable signals that could cause data to be written.
- Assert the alert output.
- Enter a terminal error state from which it does not recover until reset.

If a fatal alert is asserted by another part of the design, the module must:

- Clear all trigger and ordinary status bits.
- Deassert all active ordinary status indications.
- Prevent any new operation from starting.

The module must not release output data if an invalid mux selector, invalid sparse encoding, or internal security check failure has been detected at the same time the output data is about to be written.

## 11. Control and Trigger Register Handling

The module must clear the start, key/IV/data-input clear, output-data clear, and PRNG reseed triggers whenever their associated operations are completed. It must also clear all trigger bits when a fatal alert is asserted.

The module must allow control register updates only when idle and only if the control register does not have a storage error. Any control register update must reset the write tracking for key, IV, input data, and output status as described in Section 2.

# AES Core Module Behavioral Specification

## 1. Purpose

This module is the top-level AES core wrapper. It provides the complete AES block-cipher datapath behavior for the AES unit: accepting configuration, key, initialization vector (IV), and input data through the register interface; performing AES encryption/decryption in the supported cipher modes; managing flow control; clearing sensitive registers with pseudo-random data; and reporting security-relevant alert conditions.

The module shall support:

- AES-128, AES-192, and AES-256 encryption/decryption.
- Electronic Codebook (ECB), Cipher Block Chaining (CBC), Cipher Feedback (CFB-128), Output Feedback (OFB), and Counter (CTR) modes.
- Optional compile-time removal of AES-192 support.
- Optional first-order masked datapath for side-channel hardening.
- Optional compile-time selection of S-box implementation.
- Register-based flow control with automatic and manual operation.

## 2. Configuration-Dependent Behavior

The module has several compile-time configuration options that change its behavior:

- **AES-192 support**: When disabled, the module shall support only AES-128 and AES-256. If software selects AES-192 while support is disabled, the module shall treat the key length as AES-256.
- **Masking**: When enabled, the cipher datapath shall operate on two shares. The key is accepted through two key-share register banks, and the module shall keep the shares separate in the protected datapath. When masking is disabled, the effective key is the XOR of the two key-share banks and the cipher datapath operates on a single share.
- **S-box implementation**: All selected S-box implementations shall produce the same functional AES result; the configuration only affects timing, area, and side-channel properties.
- **Start trigger delay**: When a non-zero delay is configured, the module shall wait for that delay after a start trigger is accepted before the cipher operation begins.
- **Forcing masks to zero**: When allowed, software may force all masking randomness to zero for SCA characterization. When not allowed, this control shall be forced to zero and software writes to it shall have no effect.
- **Skip PRNG reseeding**: When enabled, the module shall skip automatic reseeding of its clearing/masking PRNGs. When disabled, the module shall obtain entropy and reseed before using the PRNGs as required.
- **Entropy width**: The width of the external entropy input is parameterizable.

## 3. Reset and Initialization

At reset, the module shall:

1. Place all internal state in a defined reset state.
2. Obtain entropy for its clearing PRNG, unless PRNG reseeding is configured to be skipped.
3. Clear all key, IV, data-input, and data-output registers with pseudo-random data.
4. Become idle only after the initialization sequence is complete.

After reset initialization is complete, the module shall be ready for software initialization.

## 4. Register Interface Behavior

### 4.1 Control Configuration

The control register is shadowed. For a control update to take effect, software must perform two writes with the same value. A mismatch between the two writes shall cause a recoverable alert and shall not update the active configuration.

The control configuration includes:

- Operation: encryption or decryption.
- Cipher mode: ECB, CBC, CFB, OFB, or CTR.
- Key length: AES-128, AES-192 if enabled, or AES-256.
- Manual-operation enable.
- Force-zero-masks enable, only if permitted by configuration.

The module shall ignore software writes to configuration, key, and IV registers when it is not idle.

Unsupported mode encodings shall be treated as no mode, and no cipher operation shall start until a valid mode is selected. Unsupported key-length encodings shall be treated as AES-256.

### 4.2 Key Registers

The initial key is provided through two 256-bit key-share register banks, each organized as eight 32-bit words.

- For all key lengths, software must write all eight words in each share bank.
- The write order is irrelevant.
- The effective key for unmasked operation is the bitwise XOR of the two share banks.
- For masked operation, the two shares are consumed by the protected datapath and must not be combined in the register-visible data path.

The module shall clear the two key-share banks with different pseudo-random data so that the cleared shares do not expose a known combined value.

### 4.3 IV Registers

The IV is provided through four 32-bit registers.

- All four registers must be written at least once before the IV is considered ready.
- The write order is irrelevant.
- The module shall update the IV registers automatically while operating in CBC, CFB, OFB, or CTR mode.
- Software shall only write new IV values while the module is idle.

### 4.4 Data Input Registers

The input data block is provided through four 32-bit registers.

- All four registers must be written at least once before an input block is considered ready.
- The write order is irrelevant.
- Data input registers may be written while the module is busy, allowing the next input block to be staged.
- After an input block is consumed by the cipher datapath, the module shall overwrite the data-input registers with pseudo-random data.

### 4.5 Data Output Registers

The output data block is provided to software through four 32-bit registers.

- The read order is irrelevant.
- In automatic mode, all four registers must be read before the module writes the next output block.
- In manual mode, the module may overwrite unread output data.

### 4.6 Trigger and Status Behavior

The module shall provide status information indicating:

- Whether the module is idle.
- Whether the input registers are ready to receive a new block.
- Whether the output registers contain a valid result.
- Whether the module is stalled due to output back-pressure.
- Recoverable alert status.
- Fatal fault status.

The module shall support trigger operations for:

- Starting a manual operation.
- Clearing key, IV, and data-input registers with pseudo-random data.
- Clearing data-output registers with pseudo-random data.
- Reseeding the clearing PRNG.

Trigger bits shall be cleared by the module when the requested trigger action has been accepted or completed.

## 5. Block Operation and Flow Control

### 5.1 Automatic Mode

By default, automatic mode is enabled.

In automatic mode, the module shall:

- Start encryption/decryption of a block whenever the input data block is ready, the IV/counter is ready if required by the mode, and the previous output block has been read.
- Stall rather than overwrite unread output data.
- Automatically continue with the next staged input block after the current block completes.

The module shall not automatically start an operation with a partially updated IV. For modes that use the IV, the IV is ready if either:

- All four IV registers have been written since the last IV update, or
- None of the IV registers have been written since the last IV update.

### 5.2 Manual Mode

When manual operation is enabled, the module shall:

- Not start automatically when input data is written.
- Start a cipher operation only when the start trigger is set, regardless of input or IV ready state.
- Not stall on unread output data; new output may overwrite previous output.

### 5.3 Key Expansion Delay

For ECB or CBC decryption, after a new key is loaded, the module shall derive and store the decryption start key before processing data blocks.

During this key-expansion phase, the module shall not process data blocks. Once the decryption start key has been derived, subsequent ECB/CBC decryptions using the same key shall start without additional delay.

Encryption operations and CFB/OFB/CTR modes do not require this decryption key-expansion phase.

## 6. Cipher Mode Behavior

The following notation is used:

- `I` = current 128-bit data input block.
- `O` = current 128-bit data output block.
- `IV` = current initialization vector or counter value.
- `E(X)` = AES forward encryption of `X`.
- `D(X)` = AES inverse decryption of `X`.
- `incr(IV)` = the 128-bit counter value incremented as an unsigned big-endian integer.

| Mode | Operation | Cipher Input | Output Block | Next IV / Counter |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ECB | Encrypt | `I` | `O = E(I)` | Not used |
| ECB | Decrypt | `I` | `O = D(I)` | Not used |
| CBC | Encrypt | `I XOR IV` | `O = E(I XOR IV)` | `O` |
| CBC | Decrypt | `I` | `O = D(I) XOR IV` | `I` |
| CFB | Encrypt | `IV` | `O = E(IV) XOR I` | `O` |
| CFB | Decrypt | `IV` | `O = E(IV) XOR I` | `I` |
| OFB | Encrypt or Decrypt | `IV` | `O = E(IV) XOR I` | `E(IV)` |
| CTR | Encrypt or Decrypt | `IV` | `O = E(IV) XOR I` | `incr(IV)` |

Clarifications:

- In CBC decryption, `IV` is the previous ciphertext block. The current ciphertext block is the data input block `I`.
- In CFB mode, the ciphertext is the value used as the next IV. During encryption the ciphertext is `O`; during decryption the ciphertext is `I`.
- In OFB mode, the next IV is the raw forward-cipher output before XOR with the data input block.
- In CTR mode, the IV register is used as the counter. It shall be incremented by one for each data block, and the updated value shall be available for the next block.

## 7. Counter Behavior

In CTR mode, the module shall implement the standard AES counter incrementing function:

- The counter value is 128 bits.
- The counter shall be treated as a big-endian integer.
- After each block is processed, the counter shall be incremented by one.
- The updated counter shall be reflected in the IV registers for use by the next block.

## 8. Security Hardening Behavior

### 8.1 Pseudo-Random Clearing

The module shall use pseudo-random data for clearing sensitive registers in order to reduce side-channel leakage.

The following shall be cleared with pseudo-random data:

- Initial key registers.
- IV registers.
- Data input registers.
- Data output registers.
- Internal cipher state after use where applicable.

The two key-share banks shall be cleared with independent pseudo-random values.

### 8.2 Shadow Control Register

The control register shall use shadow-register behavior. If the two writes of a shadowed update disagree, the module shall assert a recoverable alert and shall not update the active control value.

### 8.3 Internal Integrity Checks

The module shall protect internal control decisions, mux selections, handshake signals, and counters against fault injection.

If any internally generated protected encoding becomes invalid, the module shall:

- Treat the event as a fatal fault.
- Assert the fatal alert output.
- Enter a terminal error state.
- Stop processing and prevent further data output.
- Remain in the error state until reset.

### 8.4 Life-Cycle Escalation

When the life-cycle escalation input is asserted, the module shall treat it as a fatal security event. It shall stop operation, assert the fatal alert, and remain in the terminal error state until reset.

## 9. Alert Behavior

The module shall provide two alert outputs:

- **Recoverable alert**: Used for shadow-control-register update mismatches.
- **Fatal alert**: Used for all fatal integrity, counter, cipher-core, control, or life-cycle escalation events.

### 9.1 Recoverable Alert

A recoverable alert shall not lock up the module. The corresponding status shall be set and shall remain set until the next accepted control update, unless a fatal alert clears this recoverable status.

### 9.2 Fatal Alert

A fatal alert shall:

- Be asserted and held until reset.
- Set the fatal-fault status.
- Clear other status information.
- Place the module in a terminal error state.
- Prevent any further data output.

The module shall require a reset to exit the fatal error state.

## 10. Summary of Functional Requirements

- The module shall perform AES-128/192/256 encryption and decryption in ECB, CBC, CFB, OFB, and CTR modes.
- The module shall accept keys in two-share form through the register interface.
- The module shall provide automatic and manual block-operation flow control.
- The module shall track input, IV, and output readiness and shall not start or continue operations unless the relevant readiness conditions are satisfied.
- The module shall enforce shadow-register update semantics for control configuration.
- The module shall clear sensitive registers with pseudo-random data at reset, on clear triggers, and after use as specified.
- The module shall generate the correct IV/counter updates for all chaining modes.
- The module shall report recoverable and fatal security events through its alert outputs and status interface.
- The module shall stop and lock up on fatal faults, including life-cycle escalation and internal integrity failures, until reset.
